description: Trigger evals for screen-spec: it fires when one Figma screen frame needs a written screen spec, while screen-spec-fleet, image-to-spec, component-spec, extract-foundations-from-screens and journey-map handle many screens, an image with no Figma source, a single component, token convergence, and a multi-screen flow.

should_trigger: Can you write up the login screen from Figma? Here's the frame link, it's screen 03 and it's an auth screen.

I have the settings page frame open in Figma (node 412:88) and the developers need to build it from our component library without opening the file. Document that one screen as screen 07, controller persona, route /settings.
document the checkout confirmation frame, I want the layout, the copy, and the empty and error states written down
Design handed off the operative dashboard yesterday. Pull the frame, work out which of our components it uses, and give me a spec for that screen with the spacing mapped to our tokens.
spec this one screen from the Figma frame, shared persona, number 12

should_not_trigger.prompt: We have 14 frames for the onboarding redesign, each with a node id and a persona. Generate all the screen docs in parallel and update the screen map and routes.
There's no Figma file for this, only a PNG screenshot of the profile screen that the client emailed. Turn it into a structured spec.
Document the primary button from the Figma library: all its variants, sizes, states, motion and haptics.
All twelve screen specs now list raw hex values and pixel paddings. Converge those into color, typography and spacing role tokens without overwriting what we already curated.
Map the signup flow from welcome to first dashboard across the five screens, with the user story and the critical states along the way.
